historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (equity CAGR rejected: distorted by the FY2026 fair-value gain)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported equity 3-year CAGR of 48.1% diverges from the revenue CAGR of 28.0% by more than 30%. The cause is the FY2026 unrealised fair-value gain (about A$122M after tax); excluding it equity compounds at 33.3% (3yr) and 32.1% (5yr), in line with revenue and underlying EPS. The equity series is therefore not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs use FY2026 UNDERLYING EPS of A$1.383 (underlying NPAT A$144.7M over 104.652M diluted shares) against statutory A$0.580 (FY2023) and A$0.295 (FY2021); on statutory FY2026 EPS of A$2.536 the 3-year figure would read 63.5%, which is the fair-value gain, not earnings. FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; interest received sits in investing in every year, so no interest strip is needed): FY2021 30.470, FY2023 54.856, FY2026 114.623. Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are within 0.6pp, so SBC is not growing meaningfully faster than cash flow. FY2026 revenue growth was 22.9% reported and 28.4% in constant currency (AUD/USD averaged 0.6779 against 0.6472).

scenario_narratives.base: Visage 7 keeps winning large North American health systems at the pace of the last three years and keeps every client it has (six of six renewals in FY2026, each for a full five-year term). Contracted minimums plus exam-volume growth on transaction-based contracts carry revenue growth from 24% down through the teens as the unpenetrated share of US academic and integrated-delivery-network imaging shrinks, with cardiology and the full-stack offering (UCHealth, A$170M over ten years) extending the runway. Margins edge up from an already exceptional level; working capital stays a modest drag because large clients pay slowly. Revenue about A$1.05B in FY2036. Cross-check: management's minimum contracted revenue of A$1.3bn over the next five years (up 41%) covers about 54% of the A$2.4bn this path books over FY2027-31, before volumes above minimums, new wins and renewals.
scenario_narratives.bull: The product set broadens faster than the core market matures: cardiology and other imaging specialties, the AI platform, Visage RIS and Europe (University Hospital Heidelberg as the reference site) each become material, so constant-currency growth of around 30% holds for five years. Pricing power on renewals lifts margins toward 83% and a weaker Australian dollar turns the FY2026 currency headwind into a tailwind. Revenue about A$1.54B in FY2036. Rests on the low starting share management cites (about 11% of an estimated 690 million annual US exams) and on Digital Pathology and AI-optimised Reporting (North American release due H1 2027) raising revenue per client.
scenario_narratives.bear: The addressable pool of large US health systems is finite and several of the largest are already clients; new-contract value falls from the A$400-500M a year of FY2025-26, a well-funded competitor closes the streaming and cloud-deployment gap, and AI-native vendors or hospital consolidation give buyers leverage at renewal. Growth fades to single digits by year five, per-exam pricing and retention costs take the pre-SBC margin from 79% to 72%, and receivables keep stretching (91+ day balances already rose from A$1.0M to A$6.7M in FY2026). Still a highly profitable business; revenue about A$600M in FY2036. Named competitive axes: GE HealthCare's acquisition of Intelerad (closed March 2026) and Sectra leading net-new PACS selections; PME already serves 11 of the top 20 US hospitals. Even here the five-year revenue path (about A$2.0bn) stays above the A$1.3bn contracted minimum, so this is a slowdown case, not a contract-loss case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Pro Medicus is valued on the cash its software business produces for owners: operating cash flow less capitalised development and share-based pay, projected from components over ten years and capitalised at no more than 20x. The FY2026 fair-value gain on the 4D Medical instrument is treated as what it is, a marked-to-market asset: excluded from every flow and added once, after tax and at its lower post-balance-date mark, in the equity bridge. The business quality is not in dispute (roughly 79% EBITDA margins, no debt, 100% renewals); the valuation question is entirely how many years of 20%-plus growth the price already assumes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Duration of growth: the valuation is far more sensitive to how long 20%+ growth lasts than to any margin assumption; each scenario's value is mostly terminal.
Customer and geographic concentration: about 90% of revenue is North America, from a finite set of large health systems.
Currency: USD revenue translated to AUD; FY2026 lost A$11.8M of revenue and A$9.9M of profit to a stronger Australian dollar.
Working capital: receivables are 37% of revenue and ageing; a further stretch lowers cash conversion below the modelled level.
SBC understatement: the IFRS 2 expense (A$4.2M) is well below the market value of shares delivered at vest (A$14.9M in FY2026).
4D Medical instrument: about A$1 per share after tax in the bridge, with a value that tracks a volatile small-cap share price.

Terminal cap: a 20x cap and a 9.5% discount rate will not reproduce a market price that capitalises the business at well over 100x earnings; the gap is a finding about the price, not a calibration target.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 104,469,963 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR note 18) plus 193,451 unissued performance rights at the report date (directors' report). Ties to the diluted weighted average of 104,652,290. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report note 6(b) 'Share-based payments expense' A$4.175M (PME.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:3758, restated at :4157). No net-share-settlement tax line exists; rights are satisfied by shares issued to or bought for the Employee Share Trust.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T05:13:15Z (ASX regular close, as printed by dcf-context; to be re-verified by refresh_price.py)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5%, built in AUD: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4% plus a ~5.5-6% Australian equity risk premium at a beta near 1.0; no debt, so WACC equals cost of equity. Below the 10.5% USD-tech house default by roughly the AUD/USD risk-free differential and the absence of leverage. The same 9.5% is used in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the flows and the weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: the A$2.231M of lease liabilities is the whole of total_debt and is deducted in the net-debt bridge; lease principal (A$0.631M) is not deducted from the flows. Immaterial either way.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income was A$9.063M in FY2026 and net cash is 2.2x the FCF base, so the double-count rule applies in principle. It is recorded as 0 here because PME classifies interest received (A$9.039M) in INVESTING activities, so reported FCF (operating cash flow less capex) already excludes it; deducting it again would strip it twice. The forward EBITDA margin is likewise built on EBIT before interest.
inputs.fair_value_gain_note: FY2026 profit before tax of A$377.5M includes a A$174.24M unrealised fair-value gain on other financial assets (A$172.0M on the 4D Medical secured facility, A$2.35M on the EchoIQ subscription right). It is non-cash and non-operating: it is absent from operating cash flow, from the EBITDA series used here (A$202.3M = EBIT A$194.2M + D&A A$8.1M) and from every forward flow. Statutory EPS of A$2.536 and the A$450.9M equity balance are both inflated by it; underlying NPAT was A$144.7M (A$1.38 per diluted share). The asset itself is carried in equity_bridge at a marked-down, after-tax value.
inputs.cash_note: A$252.276M = cash and equivalents 146.482 + bank term deposits 69.644 + current other financial assets (managed funds) 36.150, all at 30 June 2026. Not adjusted for the A$38.65M FY2026 final dividend declared 18 August 2026 and since paid, nor for cash generated after balance date; the two roughly offset by the valuation date.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, three probability-weighted scenarios, via the Drivers route. Routed as an operating software company (Visage 7 enterprise imaging and Visage RIS; transaction-based contracts with minimums, 5-10 year terms) with the non-US adaptations: AUD-built WACC, a single lease treatment, and the matching-asset rule for the strategic investments. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF and no memory entry. Scenario axes are drawn from the FY2026 annual report and the Analysis JSON. No numeric FY2027 guidance exists; the only quantified forward anchor is A$1.3bn of minimum contracted revenue over five years. YEAR-1 MARGIN CHECK: the component build gives a 49.3% owner-FCF margin in FY2027 against 43.8% actual in FY2026; the gap is FY2026's unusually large receivables build (about 8% of revenue against the 2.9% modelled) and the A$1.9M currency loss, so cash conversion is the assumption most likely to prove generous. FCF BASE: reported FCF A$118.8M (OCF 127.484 less capitalised development 8.242 and plant 0.444) less SBC 4.175 = owner FCF A$114.6M, a 43.8% margin; the fair-value gain is not in it. EBITDA MARGIN PATHS ARE PRE-SBC: reported EBITDA of A$202.3M is after the A$4.2M share-based payment expense, so FY2026 pre-SBC EBITDA is A$206.5M (78.9% of revenue; 79.6% before the A$1.9M net currency loss) and the engine then deducts SBC once. SBC: the IFRS 2 charge (1.6% of revenue) understates the cost at vest, since 47,930 shares were issued to the trust at A$310.15 (A$14.9M) in FY2026; the forward path therefore rises to 2.0% rather than declining. BUYBACKS: PME is a small, regular repurchaser (A$10.1M in FY2026, A$7.9M in FY2025) and the count has been flat at ~104.5M for a decade, so the flat-count convention is funded. WORKING CAPITAL: negative capture, because growth consumes cash here: trade receivables rose A$33.5M to A$97.6M (91+ days A$6.7M from A$1.0M) and contract costs A$6.4M against a A$16.8M rise in deferred revenue, a net drag of roughly A$20M on A$48.7M of revenue growth in FY2026 (about A$5M on A$51M in FY2025, about nil in FY2024). CASH TAX: 30% throughout; the current tax charge was A$64.7M, about 31.8% of profit before tax excluding the fair-value gain, and no loss shelter exists. FY2026's 15.3% 'effective cash tax rate' KPI is an artefact of dividing cash tax by gain-inflated profit. PRICE: placeholder from the dcf-context print; refresh_price.py owns the live figure.

bear.rationale: Revenue roughly 2.3x to about A$600M by FY2036: the large-health-system market saturates, renewals reprice, and margin gives back seven points to price and to higher R&D and retention spend.

base.rationale: Revenue quadruples to about A$1.05B by FY2036. Year 1 at 24% sits between FY2026's 22.9% reported and 28.4% constant-currency growth, supported by A$407M of new contract value and A$141M of renewals signed in FY2026 and by previously won contracts scheduled to come on stream in FY2027. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin drifts from 78.9% to 81.5% on operating leverage.

bull.rationale: Revenue reaches about A$1.54B by FY2036: constant-currency growth of ~30% persists for five years as cardiology, the full-stack offering, other '-ologies' and Europe add to the North American radiology base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 20/50/30. Bear 20%: no balance-sheet or going-concern risk, but revenue is concentrated in one product sold to one customer type in one country, which is the single-dependency case for a higher bear weight. Base 50%: it already assumes a fourfold revenue increase at rising margins, which the contracted backlog and 100% retention record support. Bull 30%, not 35%: it needs several independent things to go right at once (cardiology, other specialties, Europe and pricing).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
